title: RBAC v2 Launch Checklist (Hosted + Dedicated + Private)
content:
Doc owner: Talia Benson (Program Mgmt)
Last reviewed in sync: 2025-03-21 (RBAC v2 Launch Readiness)

Purpose
- Single checklist for RBAC v2 launch readiness across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- Focus: docs + enablement, training, support readiness, telemetry/monitoring, customer communications, and compliance evidence packaging.
- This is NOT a deep technical spec; link out to Confluence/GitHub/Linear for details.

Launch definitions
- “Pilot”: feature-flagged enablement for a small set of accounts/environments with rapid rollback + dedicated support.
- “GA”: default-on for new enterprise accounts; controlled rollout for existing accounts; migration path documented.

Scope reminder (v2)
- Deny-by-default authorization checks at Gateway + service-level enforcement.
- Permission inventory + built-in role templates.
- Audit logs include authz decision context (allow/deny + why).
- Migration plan (dual-read/dual-write as needed, feature flags).

------------------------------
SECTION A — Release gating & sign-offs

A1. Sign-off checklist (must be explicitly recorded)
- [ ] Product sign-off (Naomi Feldman): PRD requirements met + scope locked for GA.
- [ ] Eng sign-off (Priya Natarajan): rollout plan approved + rollback tested.
- [ ] Security Eng sign-off (Marcus Lin): permission coverage acceptable + deny-by-default verified.
- [ ] GRC sign-off (Olga Petrov): evidence package assembled for SOC2 / enterprise questionnaires.
- [ ] Support/CS sign-off (Colin O'Donnell): playbooks, macros, and escalation paths ready.
- [ ] Release coordinator sign-off (Connor O'Brien): branching/backport plan and release notes ready.

A2. Go/No-Go meeting readiness
- [ ] Pre-read distributed (this checklist + dashboards + known risks).
- [ ] Top risks + mitigations reviewed (see risk register doc; also summarize below).
- [ ] Rollback owner + comms owner designated for launch day.

Known risks to reiterate at go/no-go
- Deny spikes due to missing role template permission (seen in Dedicated admin routing edit case).
- Private IdP group mapping misconfiguration leading to “locked out” admin.
- Stale cache decisions post role changes (needs metrics + invalidation triggers).
- “Why denied” UX exposing too much detail (must align with security guidance).

------------------------------
SECTION B — Feature flags, rollout controls, and rollback

B1. Feature flags present and documented
- [ ] Flags exist for: gateway enforcement, service enforcement, audit log authz fields, debug headers/denial reason codes, Console role mgmt UI.
- [ ] Flags support per-org and per-environment scoping (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
- [ ] Default states defined for: dev/staging/prod and Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
Owner: Connor O'Brien + Amara Diallo + Ethan Park

B2. Rollout stages defined (what flips when)
- [ ] Stage 0: internal dogfood (Redwood orgs only) — deny-by-default ON for a limited set of permissions.
- [ ] Stage 1: pilot accounts (2–5) — full RBAC v2 checks + audit decision logging ON.
- [ ] Stage 2: enterprise GA for new orgs — RBAC v2 default role templates + migrations.
- [ ] Stage 3: existing org migrations — coordinated window, monitoring, backout plan.
Owner: Talia Benson + Naomi Feldman

B3. Rollback plan validated
- [ ] 1-click rollback documented in runbook (what flags to revert; expected latency/consistency impact).
- [ ] Rollback tested in staging for: Console flows, API calls, Private installer bootstrap.
- [ ] Customer comms draft for rollback scenario prepared (internal-only + customer-facing).
Owner: Connor O'Brien + Kira Thompson

------------------------------
SECTION C — Telemetry, dashboards, alerts (launch-blocking)

C1. Required metrics emitted (by Gateway + services + Console)
- [ ] Authz decision counts: allow/deny by permission, service, route, and org.
- [ ] Denial reason code counts (top N) — confirm stable taxonomy.
- [ ] Latency impact: p50/p95/p99 for authz evaluation + request end-to-end.
- [ ] Cache metrics: hit rate, stale decision indicators (if available), TTL distribution.
- [ ] “Unannotated endpoint” / “missing permission mapping” counters (coverage gate).
Owners: Logan Wright + Allison Grant + Amara Diallo + Ethan Park

C2. Dashboards created (links to be added)
- [ ] Executive overview: denial rate trend, top denied permissions, impacted accounts.
- [ ] Engineering drill-down: per-service denial spikes; cache hit rate; error budget impact.
- [ ] Support view: org-level timeline of denies + denial reasons + correlation to role changes.
Owner: Logan Wright

C3. Alerts configured (page-worthy vs ticket-worthy)
Page (immediate):
- [ ] Deny rate > X% sustained for Y minutes for pilot/GA orgs.
- [ ] Authz evaluation failures (timeouts, dependency failures) > threshold.
- [ ] Spike in “unknown_permission” or “unmapped_endpoint” reasons.
Ticket (next business day):
- [ ] Gradual increase in denies on non-sensitive permissions.
- [ ] Elevated rate of “debug header requested” events (indicates confusion).
Owners: Fiona McCarthy + Logan Wright

C4. Logging requirements validated
- [ ] Audit logs contain required authz fields (subject, action/permission, scope, policy version, decision, denial reasons).
- [ ] Sensitive data review: denial reasons do not leak secrets/policy internals to non-admins.
Owners: Kevin Osei + Marcus Lin

------------------------------
SECTION D — Docs & customer-facing materials

D1. Docs site updates ready
- [ ] RBAC v2 conceptual overview: scopes, roles, bindings, permission model.
- [ ] Permission catalog reference + naming/versioning rules.
- [ ] Built-in role templates: recommended starting points (Hosted/Dedicated/Private variants).
- [ ] Migration guide: what changes, common breakages, how to validate.
- [ ] “Why was I denied?” troubleshooting guide.
Owners: Elliot Price + Naomi Feldman

D2. Sales/SE enablement
- [ ] Updated security FAQ entry set (RBAC + auditability + SSO interaction).
- [ ] Customer questionnaire answers include example audit log event with authz context.
- [ ] Slide(s) / 1-pager for enterprise security reviews (what’s new in v2).
Owners: Naomi Feldman + Daniel Carter

D3. Private deployment docs
- [ ] Installer/admin bootstrap steps: default admin binding and safe recovery.
- [ ] IdP mapping examples: group-to-role bindings and validation steps.
- [ ] Air-gapped / restricted environment notes (where policy bundle lives, how it updates).
Owners: Vivek Kulkarni + Colin O'Donnell

D4. Release notes
- [ ] Public release note draft (high-level behavior + admin impact) prepared.
- [ ] Internal release note with exact flags, rollout schedule, dashboards, and support escalation.
Owners: Connor O'Brien + Talia Benson

------------------------------
SECTION E — Training & internal readiness

E1. Support training (CS + Support + Solutions Eng)
- [ ] 45-minute enablement session scheduled + recorded.
- [ ] Walkthrough: diagnosing denies (permission, scope mismatch, role binding missing, stale cache).
- [ ] Common customer scenarios: read-only auditor, security admin vs billing admin separation, Private admin bootstrap.
- [ ] Escalation guide: when to involve Security Eng vs Platform vs Console.
Owners: Colin O'Donnell + Marcus Lin

E2. Engineering training (on-call + service owners)
- [ ] “How to add a permission + annotate endpoint + tests” training material distributed.
- [ ] Required patterns: deny-by-default middleware usage; consistent error semantics.
- [ ] How to interpret metrics/alerts and where to look for policy version.
Owners: Brian Murphy + Amara Diallo + Ethan Park

E3. Internal IT/admin provisioning readiness
- [ ] Redwood internal admin groups mapped (SSO groups -> RBAC roles) and tested.
- [ ] Break-glass internal process rehearsed (see Section H).
Owner: David Kim

------------------------------
SECTION F — Support readiness: macros, playbooks, and tooling

F1. Triage playbook for “permission denied”
Must include:
- [ ] Gather: org id, user id, role bindings, scope, permission string, policy version, request id.
- [ ] Check: denial reason code + whether debug header is available (admin-only).
- [ ] Determine: mis-scoped binding vs missing permission in template vs bug/regression.
- [ ] Remediation: update binding, adjust template (policy-bundle), or rollback flags.
Owner: Colin O'Donnell

F2. Ticket macros / canned responses (Support + CS)
- [ ] Macro: requesting required info (request id, timestamp, screenshot of role assignment, etc.).
- [ ] Macro: explaining scope model in plain language (org/project/env/cluster).
- [ ] Macro: Private admin lockout safe recovery steps.
Owner: Colin O'Donnell + Kira Thompson

F3. Operator tooling readiness
- [ ] Console permission viewer/search works with large permission sets.
- [ ] “Why denied” UX is present for admins and hidden/limited for standard users.
- [ ] Audit log export UI/workflow validated for Private and Hosted.
Owners: Chloe Martin + Felix Schneider + Kevin Osei

------------------------------
SECTION G — Customer communications (pilot + GA)

G1. Pilot customer comms plan
- [ ] Pilot account list finalized (name, deployment type, POC, success criteria).
- [ ] Email templates prepared: pre-enable notice, enable confirmation, and “what to watch for”.
- [ ] Shared slack channel / escalation path created for each pilot (if applicable).
Owners: Naomi Feldman + Colin O'Donnell

G2. GA comms plan
- [ ] Announcement timeline: docs live, feature enabled, migration reminders.
- [ ] Define what is “default” for new orgs vs existing orgs.
- [ ] Customer-facing FAQ: what changed about roles; how to get least privilege quickly.
Owners: Naomi Feldman + Elliot Price

G3. Known-issue disclosure guidelines
- [ ] If “debug header” exists, document who can use it (admins) and what it reveals.
- [ ] If Private bootstrap has edge cases, document safe recovery and support contact.
Owner: Marcus Lin + Vivek Kulkarni

------------------------------
SECTION H — Break-glass readiness (launch-blocking)

H1. Break-glass procedure validated
- [ ] Process documented: request, approval, time-bound elevation, monitored session.
- [ ] Who can approve: Security Eng + SecOps (as defined in break-glass doc).
- [ ] Time bound default configured (e.g., 60 min) and can’t be silently extended.
Owners: Fiona McCarthy + Marcus Lin

H2. Break-glass monitoring and alerts
- [ ] Alerting to SecOps on break-glass activation.
- [ ] Mandatory post-use review template ready and assigned owner.
Owners: Fiona McCarthy + Daniel Carter

H3. Private deployment “lockout” recovery path
- [ ] Confirm there is a documented and tested recovery path that does not require unsafe bypasses.
- [ ] Confirm audit evidence exists for any emergency access performed.
Owners: Vivek Kulkarni + Kevin Osei

------------------------------
SECTION I — Compliance evidence packaging (SOC2 + enterprise questionnaires)

I1. Evidence artifacts assembled (store in agreed evidence location)
- [ ] RBAC v2 design overview (finalized or in-review with approval trail).
- [ ] Permission inventory + classification (including ownership and update process).
- [ ] ADRs (naming/versioning; centralized vs embedded evaluation) finalized.
- [ ] Test evidence: CI coverage gates, integration tests for critical permissions.
- [ ] Audit log schema change documentation + sample redacted events.
Owners: Olga Petrov + Daniel Carter

I2. Change management evidence
- [ ] Change ticket(s)/PRs with approvals linked (Gateway middleware, audit log fields, policy bundle generation).
- [ ] Rollout runbook + observed metrics from pilot (deny rate, incidents, support tickets).
- [ ] Incident postmortem summary included if relevant (streaming endpoint bypass hotfix reference).
Owners: Daniel Carter + Connor O'Brien

I3. Access control control-mapping (SOC2 alignment)
- [ ] Map RBAC v2 features to relevant controls (least privilege, access review, logging/monitoring).
- [ ] Confirm audit logs are retained per policy and exportable to SIEM with authz context.
Owners: Olga Petrov + Kevin Osei

I4. Customer questionnaire packet
- [ ] Standard answers updated (granularity, scopes, separation of duties, audit log fields).
- [ ] Provide a sample “Read-only auditor” role template explanation.
- [ ] Provide a sample denial reason explanation that is safe and non-sensitive.
Owners: Naomi Feldman + Daniel Carter

------------------------------
SECTION J — Final “day-of-launch” checklist (run-of-show)

T-7 days
- [ ] Confirm pilot readiness: flags staged, dashboards live, support trained.
- [ ] Confirm docs drafts reviewed by Security + Product.

T-2 days
- [ ] Freeze permission catalog changes except emergency fixes.
- [ ] Confirm on-call schedule includes knowledgeable responders (Gateway + Control Plane + Console + Security).

T-0 (launch)
- [ ] Turn on flags per plan (record exact time + scope).
- [ ] Monitor denial rate + top denial reasons + latency.
- [ ] Support channel staffed for rapid triage.

T+1 day
- [ ] Summarize metrics: deny rates, support ticket volume, regressions.
- [ ] Decide whether to expand rollout ring.

T+1 week
- [ ] Post-launch review: what broke, docs gaps, role template changes required.
- [ ] Update evidence package with real-world monitoring outputs.

------------------------------
Open questions / to-dos (as of 2025-03-22)
- [ ] Confirm default deny rate thresholds for paging vs ticketing in Hosted vs Private (Logan + Fiona).
- [ ] Confirm whether any denial reasons should be hidden even for org admins (Marcus + Naomi).
- [ ] Confirm “auditor” template includes audit log export permission across Private/Dedicated consistently (Kevin + Vivek).
- [ ] Confirm migration docs include exact mapping from RBAC v1 roles to v2 templates (Naomi + Benji).

Change log
- 2025-02-04: Created checklist (Talia).
- 2025-03-02: Added compliance evidence packaging section + SIEM export requirements (Daniel/Kevin).
- 2025-03-14: Added break-glass monitoring + Private lockout recovery emphasis (Fiona/Vivek).
- 2025-03-22: Updated day-of launch run-of-show + clarified training owners (Talia).
